sovereign_country.strategic_role: 苏伊士运河经济特区、辐射中东及北非的低成本轻工制造

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Publishing of Massively Multiplayer Online Role-Playing Games

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid: Civil Law (Napoleonic-based) with Islamic Sharia as the principal source of legislation and limited residual common-law practice in economic/free-zone matters

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law No. 159 of 1981 (Egyptian Companies Law), as amended by Law No. 4 of 2018, Limited Liability Company chapter (arts. 85-126), read with Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 and GAFI Executive Regulations; notarization is governed by Authentication and Audit Law No. 68 of 1947.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) - One-Stop Shop (OSS) for Company Establishment, Ministry of Investment and International Cooperation, in coordination with the Commercial Registry Division.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Memorandum of Association (Aqd at-Ta'sis) and Articles of Association (an-Nizam al-Asasi), executed before a licensed Notary Public and deposited through the GAFI One-Stop Shop Company Registration Application (OSS Form 2).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is imposed on an Egyptian LLC under Law 159/1981 as amended; however, the allotted quotas must be fully subscribed, and GAFI requires a Capital Deposit Certificate from a Central Bank of Egypt-licensed bank showing the full deposit in the LLC's under-formation account. No mandatory escrow account exists; funds are released to the company's free operating account after the incorporation certificate issues. In-kind contributions are permitted subject to independent valuation, notarization, and inclusion in the founding contract.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED 1) The Memorandum and Articles of Association of the LLC, authenticated by the Notary Public, are ratified and adopted. 2) All quota interests subscribed by the founding quotaholders are allotted per the capital schedule annexed to the founding contract. 3) The registered office is fixed at the address set out in the lease exhibited to GAFI and is hereby confirmed as the company's seat. 4) The founding quotaholder named in Schedule 1 is appointed General Manager and sole legal representative, with authority to sign, open bank accounts, and bind the Company. 5) The founding quotaholder named in Schedule 2 is appointed Corporate Secretary for registration and licensing filings. 6) The General Manager is authorized to pay all incorporation fees and complete every filing before GAFI, the Commercial Registry, the Civil Defense Authority, and the EEAA.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Reservation and Cover Name Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI One-Stop Shop - Name Reservation Window (physical or GAFI digital portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File OSS Form 1 requesting reservation of the proposed English and Arabic company names; GAFI verifies uniqueness against the Commercial Registry index and protects against confusingly similar marks; a Name Reservation Certificate valid for 60 days is issued.
required_dossiers: Completed GAFI Name Reservation Form 1
Draft Memorandum of Association stating proposed names
Copies of founding quotaholders' national IDs or passports
Notarized power of attorney if an administrative agent files
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for similarity or public-order conflict, file an alternative name within the same application window; an administrative objection may be lodged with the GAFI Legal Opinion Directorate within 15 days of the rejection notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of the Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Justice Notary Public Office (Authentication Division of the Real Estate Registration and Authentication Authority)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: All quotaholders or their legal representatives must appear before the notary to execute the Arabic founding contract; foreign corporate quotaholders must present apostilled board resolutions and powers of attorney; the notary authenticates signatures, fixes the contractual date, and issues the certified instrument required for commercial registration.
required_dossiers: Final draft Memorandum and Articles of Association (Arabic original plus English translation)
Certified passports and national IDs of all quotaholders and signatories
Apostilled/certified board resolution and power of attorney for any foreign corporate quotaholder
Name Reservation Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary refuses authentication for missing or defective documentation, cure the defect by re-submitting the complete file, including legalized translations; a wrongful refusal may be challenged before the competent urgent matters court within 10 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit of Subscription Capital and Issuance of Capital Deposit Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Any Central Bank of Egypt-licensed commercial bank (Capital Deposit Desk) selected by the founders
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary corporate account in the name of the company under formation using the reserved name; deposit the full allotted cash capital, and instruct the bank to issue a Capital Deposit Certificate addressed to GAFI; the certificate must show the account number, company name under formation, and deposited amount, and must remain valid through the registration date.
required_dossiers: Name Reservation Certificate
Notarized copy of the founding contract (or draft proof for account opening)
Passports and IDs of authorized signatories
Source-of-funds declaration and anti-money-laundering questionnaire required by the bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a bank rejects the account opening due to insufficient AML clearance, provide an enhanced source-of-wealth statement or choose another CBE-licensed bank; any refusal based on non-resident status may be escalated to the bank's compliance officer, who must rule in writing within 5 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: GAFI One-Stop Shop Registration and Issuance of Incorporation Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI One-Stop Shop - Company Registration Directorate
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the full consolidation file to the OSS officer; GAFI conducts the statutory verification of the founding contract, capital certificate, registered office, and quotaholders' eligibility; upon clearance, GAFI stamps the founding contract, enrolls the LLC in the Commercial Registry, and issues the Certificate of Incorporation, the Commercial Registry Extract, and the initial Tax Card through the single transaction windows.
required_dossiers: Notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association
Capital Deposit Certificate from the bank
Name Reservation Certificate
Certified copy of the registered office lease or ownership deed, with the lease executed on a registered or stamped form accepted by GAFI
GAFI OSS Form 2 (Company Registration Application)
Passports and IDs of managers and quotaholders
Vote/consent schedules confirming quota allotment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If GAFI issues a correction notice, the founders have 30 days to cure by filing an amended supplementary resolution or missing certificates; an unjustified refusal or delay may be appealed to the GAFI Investment Complaints Unit under Law 72 of 2017, and a clean-hands applicant may seek an administrative injunction before the State Council.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Employment, Social Insurance, and Premises Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Manpower - Labor Office; National Organization for Social Insurance; local district (Hay/Markaz) commercial licensing office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 30 days of the commercial registry date, enroll the LLC and its employees with the applicable social insurance office, file the labor force register, and appoint the workplace safety representative; concurrently obtain the Governorate-issued Commercial Premises Permit (Rekhsat al-Mahall) and the Civil Defense fire-safety clearance for the physical office address.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and Commercial Registry Extract
Tax Card and statistical card issued at the OSS
Registered lease and building safety certificate
Managers' and employees' labor contracts and IDs
Social insurance enrollment forms (forms 1 and 2)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late filings are corrected through voluntary disclosure submissions; social insurance and labor registrations may be remediated within the first 30 days with nominal late fees; if the district refuses the premises permit due to building classification, substitute a compliant commercial address and re-file the permit.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Industrial Development Authority (IDA) - Licensing Sector, Ministry of Trade and Industry, acting under Industrial Licensing Law No. 15 of 2017
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Industrial Activity Classification Confirmation (Non-Industrial Digital Services Exemption Certificate) - confirming that software publishing and MMORPG distribution under ISIC 5820 is not an industrial manufacturing activity and therefore requires no industrial operating license; the operative trading authority derives from the Commercial Registry Extract and the Governorate-issued Commercial Premises Permit.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency (EEAA) - Ministry of Environment, acting under Law No. 4 of 1994 as amended by Law No. 9 of 2009
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category C (White List / Registration Tier) - the software publishing office activity requires only an environmental self-assessment registration (Form B) and an environmental commitment statement for the office premises; no full EIA study is mandated.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater or point-source VOC emissions are generated by pure software operations; sanitary effluent must comply with Law 93 of 1962 and Ministry of Housing Decree No. 44 of 2000 for discharge to public sewers; electronic waste including decommissioned servers and batteries must be transferred to licensed recyclers under Waste Management Law No. 202 of 2020; any standby diesel generator must observe Law 4 of 1994 ambient air quality ceilings and obtain EEAA registration.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: The General Administration of Civil Defense (Ministry of Interior) must issue a fire-safety certificate for the registered office, conditioned on fire extinguishers, emergency exits, signage, and an approved evacuation plan; the Governorate buildings directorate must certify structural load adequacy for the occupied floor; the Ministry of Manpower performs occupational safety and health inspection under Labor Law No. 12 of 2003, requiring a workplace registration statement and, for offices above 50 employees, a dedicated safety officer.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) under the Ministry of Finance; official registration, e-filing and e-invoicing portal: https://www.eta.gov.eg (unified tax portal; e-invoicing platform at https://invoicing.eta.gov.eg)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned Egyptian LLC must obtain a single unified Tax Identification Number (TIN) through ETA's consolidated registration procedure: (1) incorporate with the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) and obtain commercial registry extract from the Ministry of Commerce; (2) execute a notarized power of attorney appointing a resident general manager or statutory representative; (3) submit through the ETA unified registration portal the certified articles of association, commercial registration, proof of address, bank account details, and board/owner resolutions; (4) complete income tax, VAT, payroll (salary tax), stamp tax and real estate tax registrations simultaneously; (5) receive the consolidated TIN certificate within approximately ten business days of a complete submission; non-resident principals with a taxable presence in Egypt must also register through a designated tax representative or fixed establishment.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Egypt does not apply US-style check-the-box elections. The Egyptian LLC is mandatorily classified as a resident juridical person taxed at the entity level under Income Tax Law No. 91 of 2005, as substantially amended by Law No. 27 of 2022 (headline CIT rate 25% for resident companies). Available statutory elections include: (i) group consolidation election for wholly-owned Egyptian subsidiaries, subject to ETA pre-approval; (ii) joint venture election under Law No. 27 of 2022 to tax an undivided venture as a standalone entity; (iii) branch versus subsidiary primary establishment election for foreign enterprises; and (iv) advance pricing agreements for transfer pricing certainty. No hybrid mismatch check-the-box election is available under Egyptian domestic law.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under Law No. 67 of 2016, as amended
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EGP 500,000 annual value of taxable supplies (mandatory VAT registration threshold for local suppliers; non-resident persons making taxable supplies in Egypt through a fixed establishment or reliant on the reverse-charge mechanism are also required to register regardless of turnover)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: E-invoicing and e-receipts are mandatory on a phased basis for taxpayers meeting ETA turnover thresholds, including digital platform operators and software publishers. Invoices must be generated through ETA-approved software or direct API integration, digitally signed with the ETA seller certificate, transmitted to the ETA e-invoice platform in near real-time using JSON/XML fiscal records, validated by the ETA engine, and stamped with an ETA-generated QR or clearance code before issuance to the buyer. An invoice failing to obtain ETA clearance is legally treated as an unissued invoice and attracts delay fines plus non-deductibility of input VAT.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to: (a) goods actually exported from Egypt and customs-cleared for exit; (b) services rendered for non-resident customers and consumed wholly outside Egypt, including electronically supplied, digital, and MMORPG online game-publishing services delivered via app store platforms to non-resident players; (c) services, financial, or digital supplies supporting export transactions. Claimant must prove that the service is performed and delivered outside Egypt, that payment is received in foreign currency from the non-resident purchaser, that the buyer is not registered for Egyptian VAT, and that no economic use of the supply occurs in Egypt.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Bayaniya) with actual exit stamp
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill
Inward Remittance Certificate evidencing foreign-exchange repatriation
Export contract or digital services subscription/payout agreement
App store financial statements (Apple App Store and Google Play payout reports) linked to the non-resident purchase trail
ETA zero-rated e-invoice with QR/clearance stamp
Summary of export transactions attached to the periodic VAT return (Form 24 equivalent)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: ETA audit scrutiny extends to export documentation for the five-year statutory limitation period and longer in cases of fraud. Penalties include a VAT evasion fine equal to double the tax evaded with a statutory minimum, incremental delay fines for late or incomplete e-invoice clearance, fines of EGP 3,000 up to EGP 50,000 per non-cleared e-invoice, and criminal liability risk including imprisonment under Articles 71 and 73 of Law No. 67 of 2016. Export zero-rating is retrospectively clawed back with interest where foreign currency is not received within the 180-day repatriation deadline or where the underlying customs, remittance, or payout documentation is forged or materially inaccurate.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) — the sole national monetary and foreign-exchange authority under Law No. 194 of 2020 (Promulgating the Central Bank and Banking System Law), its Executive Regulations, and the supporting CBE foreign-exchange circulars. All foreign-currency dealings by resident Egyptian entities must be executed exclusively through CBE-authorized banks; unofficial market FX transactions or offshore settlement rings for Egyptian export proceeds are statutorily prohibited and criminally sanctionable. The Ministry of Finance, the Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA), and the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) are the ancillary regulators for tax and capital-account matters.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Egypt operates a unified, market-determined exchange rate (managed float) since the CBE alignment decision of 6 March 2024, which removed the previous parallel-market spread and is anchored by Egypt's IMF Extended Fund Facility. Current-account transactions — software and digital-gaming service exports, in-app purchase proceeds, foreign-currency operating receipts, and dividends/profit remittances — are freely convertible through authorized banks, subject to documentary verification (platform payout reports, ETA tax clearance, audited financials, and CBE balance-of-payments purpose codes). Profit remittance hurdles include obtaining an ETA tax clearance certificate, evidencing the original USD inflow by bank advice, and ensuring the benefiting bank account matches the Apple/Google payout beneficiary name. Capital-account transactions are not automatically convertible: inward share-capital injections, shareholder loans, and acquisition of Egyptian assets must be routed through authorized banks under declared CBE purpose codes, and outward repatriation of original capital requires proof of the originating inflow, updated Commercial Registry/GAFI filings, and audited statements. In practice, banks apply net-open-position discipline, EGP liquidity constraints, and require Arabic-notarized corporate documentation before releasing large FX conversions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Digital-gaming and software-export proceeds (classified under CBE balance-of-payments services exports) must be repatriated through an authorized Egyptian bank within 180 days from the date of the export invoice/shipment per CBE foreign-exchange instructions issued under Law No. 194 of 2020. Following the 6 March 2024 liberalization, the CBE no longer prescribes a fixed mandatory conversion ratio: exporters may retain the full foreign-currency amount in an onshore foreign-currency account at the receiving authorized bank or convert into EGP at the interbank rate; alternatively, proceeds may be netted against documented import or credit obligations with bank approval. The collecting bank must record the inflow in the CBE reporting framework, the exporter must file the applicable proceeds declaration within 30 days of receipt, and any retention offshore, unreported offset, or conversion outside the authorized banking channel constitutes a CBE violation. Consequently, the EG_LLC must direct all Apple App Store and Google Play payouts via SWIFT directly to its Egyptian USD account and maintain a complete audit trail from Store Connect payout reports to bank credits.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Multi-Currency Account (USD/EGP) for service-export proceeds and treasury operations
Operational Foreign-Currency Account (USD) plus EGP current account with export-proceeds desk
Operational USD/EGP account with digital FX platform, SWIFT banking, and dedicated MNB desk
Multi-currency operational account (USD/GBP/EUR), preferred for Apple/Google USD wires via HSBC global correspondent network
Operational USD/EGP corporate account with trade-finance ancillary limits
Operational corporate account with USD treasury support and product flexibility

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: LOW — legally constrained for the EG_LLC as a resident Egyptian entity. Resident legal entities are not permitted to use unlicensed or offshore electronic-money institutions (Wise, Payoneer, Airwallex, Revolut Business, or similar) as the primary collection or settlement rail for service-export proceeds. All export receipts must be repatriated through an authorized CBE bank; interposing an offshore EMI ring-fence would breach the CBE foreign-exchange instructions under Law 194/2020, distort the export-proceeds reporting obligation, and materially increase the risk of corporate account rejection or regulatory inquiry. Locally licensed Egyptian fintech payment providers (licensed by the CBE under the retail-payment regulatory framework) may support EGP merchant collection and payout automation, but they do not replace a Tier-1 bank for USD/EGP cross-border clearance. The recommended architecture is direct SWIFT settlement from Apple/Google to the onshore Tier-1 bank; an offshore parent entity, if any, may use EMIs only for incidental non-Egyptian treasury functions, never for the EG_LLC's export proceeds.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is mandatory for corporate account origination. All Tier-1 Egyptian banks require at least one natural-person signatory or director — Egyptian-resident or non-resident — to attend the branch in person, sign the account-opening forms, and complete the compliance KYC interview; remote or fully digital onboarding is not available as a substitute for an LLC with a cross-border service-export profile and foreign-currency settlement. A non-resident director may delegate authority by an original notarized power of attorney legalized by the Egyptian Consulate and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, authorizing a resident manager to attend the interview and operate the account. The bank will additionally require an LLC board resolution approving the account, the authorized signatories, and the electronic-banking mandates. Practical planning: schedule the initial in-branch visit with the General Manager and all signatories, present corporate documents in Arabic/English with apostilled or legalized originals, and budget 10–15 business days for compliance vetting before account activation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficiary-name mismatch between Apple App Store / Google Play payout reports and the LLC's bank account beneficiary — remitters are Apple Distribution International Ltd (Ireland) and Google Ireland Ltd / Google Asia Pacific Pte. Ltd, not the EG_LLC itself.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide (i) Apple Store Connect Payments & Financial Reports for the trailing 12 months showing the EG_LLC as payee; (ii) the executed Apple Developer Program License Agreement and Google Play Developer Distribution Agreement; (iii) prior bank statements evidencing settlement from the same remitters; (iv) a signed beneficiary-ownership declaration; and (v) the remitters' VAT/registration identifiers with negative-media and sanctions-screening reports.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) opacity or shell-company red flags arising from non-resident or multi-tier ownership of the Egyptian LLC.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver the up-to-date Egyptian Commercial Registry extract, notarized Articles of Association in Arabic/English, the statutory UBO register identifying all natural persons holding 25% or more (with national ID/passport copies and address proof), a group-structure organogram, the ETA Tax Card and VAT registration certificate, and a signed confidentiality waiver enabling the bank to verify the source of wealth of each UBO.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Digital-gaming fraud and money-laundering indicators — chargebacks, stolen-card-funded in-app purchases, and layering through virtual currency or in-game tokens.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the platform fraud framework (Apple/Google Hosted Commerce controls, anti-fraud rules, refund and chargeback thresholds below 0.5%), quarterly chargeback and refund statistics segregated by store, IP-geolocation and payment-device consistency monitoring outputs, the LLC's Transaction Monitoring and Suspicious Activity Reporting policy, and a board-approved Anti-Fraud Attestation confirming no acceptance of fraudulent proceeds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign-exchange compliance suspicion: cash conversion of USD into EGP, receipt of proceeds via an unlicensed EMI, or unreported offsets outside the CBE reporting framework.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Execute a Foreign-Currency Proceeds Undertaking committing the LLC to receive all Apple/Google settlements via SWIFT in USD only, retain funds in the bank's USD account, and convert solely at the interbank rate through the bank; attach a 12-month USD/EGP cash-flow projection, copies of prior CBE purpose-code declarations, and the bank's CBE-format confirmation that no unreported offshore balances exist.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions or politically-exposed-person (PEP) screening matches affecting directors, beneficial owners, remitters, or jurisdictions of incorporation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Supply negative screening results for the LLC, its UBOs, all signatories, and material counterparties against OFAC SDN, EU, UN, and local Egyptian sanctions lists; completed PEP and source-of-wealth questionnaires for any PEP-tagged individual; a negative media-search report; and a written commitment to maintain constant enhanced monitoring under the bank's AML terms.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Equity contributions: foreign shareholders must remit by SWIFT MT103 only, using the bank's incoming-wire details, with the beneficiary field naming the EG_LLC and the payment reference stating share capital contribution. The receiving Egyptian bank posts the credit to the operational USD account and records the CBE balance-of-payments purpose code for direct-investment equity in a resident company. The LLC must then file the corresponding capital increase with the Egyptian Commercial Registry and, if GAFI-registered, with GAFI within the statutory filing window (generally 30 days from the shareholders' resolution), presenting the updated Commercial Registry extract to the bank. Shareholder or subordinated loans: remit as intercompany financing under the appropriate CBE purpose code, attaching the executed loan agreement, commercial interest-rate evidence, and repayment schedule; the bank registers the exposure in CBE monitoring, and later principal and interest repayment requires an outward remittance referencing the original inward advice. All injections must be supported by the remitter's bank reference, the LLC board resolution, and the shareholders' resolution; the bank performs expected-use verification and retains the transfer receipt for future profit repatriation matching.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Operational disbursements (cloud infrastructure, ad networks, licensing, contractors, influencers): settled by SWIFT MT103 in USD/EUR/GBP via the authorized Egyptian bank's correspondent network, each payment carrying the applicable CBE purpose code (computer/software services, royalties, marketing) and supporting invoices; the bank applies liquidity and net-open-position limits with CBE post-transaction reporting. For physical procurement (merchandising, hardware, colocation equipment), the LLC may open an Irrevocable Documentary Letter of Credit under its import-finance line, with commercial invoice, packing list, bill of lading, and certificate of origin presented; for pure digital MMORPG content, direct SWIFT MT103 vendor payments with a comfort-letter framework are standard and faster than LC processing. Dividend and profit remittances to foreign shareholders: executed by outward SWIFT MT103 under the profit-repatriation purpose code, conditional on audited financial statements, an ETA tax clearance certificate, confirmation that the distribution corresponds to declared net after-tax reserves, and a board resolution; any EGP conversion occurs at the interbank rate inside the bank. Local EGP clearing is conducted via the CBE RTGS system, while USD clearing for the LLC's receipts and payments is settled over SWIFT through the bank's London or New York correspondent accounts.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable plain-vanilla FX forwards (USD/EGP) for underlying export proceeds and import commitments, tenor typically up to 12 months, executed with the authorized bank under a master ISDA/IFEMA-style treasury line.
FX swaps (USD/EGP and USD/GBP/EUR crosses) for liquidity and receivables/payables management with an underlying commercial transaction.
Cross-currency swaps for longer-term USD/EGP or USD/EUR exposures arising from licensing and royalty streams.

Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in the London/global market — permissible only for the non-Egyptian parent as a translation hedge; the resident EG_LLC must not execute offshore NDFs because onshore dealers operate on a deliverable-only basis and the CBE has not licensed an onshore NDF market.

Interest-rate swaps (IRS) ancillary to the bank's term-lending facilities; speculative, uncollateralized, or crypto-denominated hedges (USDT or other stablecoin conversions) are prohibited by the CBE and must never be used by the LLC.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Tax Return and Audited Financial Statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA), Ministry of Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months after the end of the company's fiscal year; for a calendar-year LLC, due by 30 April. Extension available only for consolidated groups with prior approval.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment surcharge of 2% per month on unpaid corporate income tax, capped at 20%; non-filing penalties up to EGP 50,000; potential attachment of bank accounts and administrative revocation of tax registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Commercial Registry Renewal (Qayd Tijari renewal)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registry Office operating under the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually during January for the calendar year; the updated commercial extract must be obtained before the end of January.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal fine of EGP 100 per month up to EGP 2,000; after two consecutive unrenewed years, the commercial registry may strike off the LLC and GAFI may commence compulsory dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Central Agency for Public Mobilization and Statistics (CAPMAS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 January, covering the preceding calendar year's activity (headcount, establishment data, revenue indicators).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine for non-filing or false data up to EGP 20,000; refusal of CAPMAS clearance which may block renewal of business licenses and registry approvals.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Egyptian law requires every LLC to maintain audited annual financial statements; a small LLC with paid-in capital below EGP 100,000 and annual revenue below EGP 500,000 may file a reviewed financial summary, but the ETA may require full audit for cross-border digital payments. Audits must be performed by a certified auditor registered with the Egyptian Financial Regulatory Authority (FRA).
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS), substantially converged with IFRS, issued by the Ministry of Investment and supervised by the Egyptian Society of Accountants and Auditors.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Law No. 80/2002 on Combating Money Laundering, the LLC must maintain and update a beneficial ownership register. The annual confirmation is performed at the ordinary general meeting by validating share transfers and updating the register if ownership of 25% or more has changed. Share transfers must be reflected in the share transfer ledger and any resulting ownership change notified to GAFI within 30 days.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $2,000–$6,000 per year for a cross-border MMORPG publishing LLC

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general CIT holiday for MMORPG or software publishing in Egypt. The Egyptian LLC is taxed on worldwide net income under Law 91/2005 as amended. Actual business expenses, depreciation, and amortisation of intangible assets are deductible. Investment Law 72/2017 incentives may benefit physical industrial projects in designated zones, not digital commerce income. No preferential CIT rate applies to in-app purchase revenue.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Egypt Corporate Income Tax Return Form 19 (Bayyan 19), filed electronically through the Egypt Tax Authority (ETA) e-tax portal (tax.gov.eg / e-invoicing integration).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within four months after the close of the fiscal year; for a calendar-year LLC, by 30 April of the following year. For an approved non-calendar fiscal year, the deadline is four months after that year-end. Advance CIT payments are made on an estimated quarterly/monthly basis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer legal name, tax card number, commercial registration number, legal form, fiscal year-end, address, directors, and authorised signatory details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: List all non-resident shareholders and ultimate beneficial owners in the ownership schedule; attach a board resolution appointing an Egyptian resident manager or tax representative when required.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue from MMORPG operations, including Apple App Store and Google Play payouts, in-app purchases, subscriptions, virtual currency sales, cosmetic item sales, and licensing fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile net platform remittances to gross retail sales; attach platform payout statements and show separately revenue from Egyptian users and foreign users; do not net Apple/Google commissions unless properly recorded as deductible platform fees.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Game development costs, server hosting, staff salaries, marketing and user acquisition, IP royalty or licence fees paid to related parties, professional fees, depreciation, and general administrative expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expenses recharged by a non-resident parent or affiliate must meet Egyptian arm's length rules and documentary evidence requirements; withholding tax exposure must be analysed before treating service or royalty payments as deductible.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 : Taxable income and discontinued expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting profit reconciled to taxable profit: non-deductible expenses, depreciation differences, transfer pricing adjustments, and tax losses carried forward within the 5-year limit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If treaty or PE arguments affect Egyptian source income, attach a legal memorandum and supporting contemporaneous evidence; the ordinary reconciliation schedule remains mandatory for the resident LLC.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 : Tax credits and advance payments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax withheld at source on dividends, interest, and royalties; foreign tax credits; quarterly advance CIT instalments paid during the year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach Tax Residency Certificates and treaty relief approvals for any foreign taxes claimed; credits are allowed only for taxes actually paid and covered by valid ETA receipts.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 : Tax due and authorised declaration
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computed CIT at 22.5% on taxable income, less credits and instalments; net tax payable; declaration of controlled transactions and transfer pricing documentation status.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The authorised Egyptian representative or managing director must sign under penalty of false declarations; a non-resident director's signature must be supported by notarised power of attorney unless waived by ETA practice.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of Form 19 triggers a fixed penalty plus monthly delay surcharge on the unpaid tax, effectively accruing daily. Non-filed returns allow the ETA to assess on an estimation basis and deny deduction claims. Deliberate under-reporting constitutes tax evasion carrying an additional penalty of up to 100% of the evaded tax, imprisonment up to five years, and restitution orders.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke the reduced or exempt DTA rate, the non-resident beneficial owner must obtain a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from its home tax authority; complete the ETA beneficial ownership declaration; submit the treaty relief application to the Egyptian withholding agent before the dividend distribution or payment; the Egyptian entity must obtain ETA confirmation or file the withholding return using the treaty position. Where treaty relief is not applied at source, the non-resident must submit a refund claim within the statutory time limits, attaching TRC, source documentation, and evidence of economic substance.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory WHT on royalties paid to non-residents is 20%; statutory WHT on interest is 20%. Egypt's DTAs typically reduce royalty withholding to 0%–15% and interest to 0%–15%, commonly 5%–10%, depending on the treaty, recipient type, beneficial ownership, and domestic substance conditions.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EGP 10,000,000 per annum in aggregate related-party transactions triggers mandatory Egyptian Local File documentation; the Master File is required when the multinational group's consolidated revenue exceeds EGP 500,000,000; group CbCR filing applies at the ultimate parent threshold established by Egyptian law (OECD-equivalent).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Egypt has no separate Economic Substance Regulations regime in the UAE sense; however, the Income Tax Law, ETA practice, and judicial anti-abuse principles require the EG LLC to demonstrate genuine commercial substance: real staff, management and control in Egypt, actual business risk, and substantive game development or publishing functions. A shell LLC claiming DTA benefits or deducting large royalty flows without substance is vulnerable to recharacterisation, denial of treaty benefits, and imposition of Egyptian-source withholding taxes.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Understating Apple/Google gross payouts, keeping parallel books, deleting financial records, fabricating development expenses, or filing Form 19 with false revenue declarations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Egyptian Income Tax Law 91/2005: fine of up to 100% of the evaded tax, monthly delay surcharges, imprisonment up to five years, asset seizure, and revocation of tax registration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, officers and signatories who knowingly participate are jointly and severally liable; the court may issue travel bans, freeze personal assets, and impose criminal imprisonment notwithstanding the LLC's limited liability shield.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company / absence of commercial substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: EG LLC has no office, no employees, no management meetings in Egypt, no control over operations, and exists solely to hold Apple/Google developer accounts or route royalties to offshore related parties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ETA may disregard the shell, treat the foreign parent as having a deemed Egyptian permanent establishment, deny DTA benefits, impose 20% dividend/royalty withholding, and make transfer pricing adjustments with penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Nominee directors and foreign beneficial owners are exposed to veil-piercing: civil restitution, travel bans, freezing of foreign and domestic assets, and potential criminal liability for abuse of legal form.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying excessive royalty or licence fees to a related foreign entity for MMORPG IP without benchmarking; cross-border cost allocations without actual services or development functions; failing to prepare Local File when related-party transactions exceed EGP 10,000,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ETA will recompute the controlled transaction at arm's length; additional CIT is assessed with monthly delay surcharge; failure to submit TP documentation results in evidence-limiting penalties and potential assessment based on available information.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: CFO, tax director, and members of the board who approve false TP documentation can be named as defendants in criminal tax proceedings; personal fines and imprisonment apply where the misstatement is intentional.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / financial sanctions / platform payout misuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the Egyptian LLC's bank account as a conduit for app-store payouts to conceal beneficial ownership; permitting in-game virtual currency transfers to sanctioned persons; failing to conduct any AML/KYC checks on high-volume payment rails.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Egyptian AML Law as amended by Law 18/2021: imprisonment of three to ten years, fines from EGP 100,000 to EGP 1,000,000, freezing orders, and closure of the payment account; Apple and Google developer accounts may also be terminated.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers are personally liable for wilful AML violations; travel bans, bank freezes, personal fines, and confiscation orders can be issued against individuals irrespective of the corporate entity's liability.
